Chapter 7: Seeking Guidance—Hearing God’s Voice in Everyday Decisions.
Life’s full of crossroads, isn’t it? Those moments when you stand at a fork in the road, feeling the pressure of making just the right choice. It could be a career move you’re considering, a tricky parenting dilemma, or simply wondering, “What’s my purpose here?” That longing for guidance—it can be almost overwhelming sometimes. I mean, who hasn’t wished for a clear sign from above, or maybe just a little guarantee that you won’t mess it all up?
Let me share a story. There was a woman facing a huge decision: should she relocate her family? She did everything—made pro and con lists, asked friends for advice, researched every possible option. But, instead of finding clarity, her anxiety only got worse. In her prayers, she pleaded with God for an answer. She expected something dramatic, maybe a voice or a sign. But what she actually noticed was much quieter—a gentle sense of peace about one particular choice. It didn’t even make much sense on paper, but deep down, it just felt right.
Isn’t it interesting how often God’s guidance comes in the quiet moments? Sometimes it’s not a lightning bolt, but more like a steady calm, or a persistent idea that keeps coming back. For her, it meant tuning in—not just to her own feelings, but also to wisdom she found in Scripture, conversations with trusted friends, and even those little “coincidences” that seemed to point the way.
There’s another woman who wondered if she should go back to school after years away. She brought all her hopes and fears into her prayers, asking God for both courage and a sign she was on the right track. Instead of one big answer, she started noticing doors opening—like scholarships, mentors who believed in her, and a spark of purpose that just wouldn’t go away. Looking back, she realized God’s guidance had been woven into the journey all along, showing up in ways she never expected.
Here’s something to think about: seeking guidance in prayer isn’t about demanding certainty or making life risk-free. It’s really about inviting God into your decision-making process, and trusting that even if you take a wrong turn, it can still help you grow. The more you practice this habit, the easier it becomes to recognize God’s leading—not as a booming voice, but as a steady presence, quietly guiding your steps.
Over time, that fear of making the “wrong” choice starts to fade. It’s replaced by a new kind of confidence—a sense that God’s with you, whatever happens. Decisions stop being about getting everything perfect, and become more about partnership—walking side by side with God, through every twist and turn.
